_comment: Published maturity status of the temporary/ add-ons (TODO P2-2). ci/check-addon-maturity.sh checks this file against the tree on every gate run; docs/ADDONS.md 'Maturity' is the readable form. An add-on leaves 'experimental' only with every 'open' item closed and an operator approval recorded under 'promotion' (see 'criteria').

criteria.choice: standard: a 14-day soak for beta, then 30 days enforcing for stable

beta.soak: monitor (log) mode on a real host that is not a test machine, for at least 14 consecutive days, with the add-on's alerts shipped off the host
beta.alerts: every alert raised during the soak is explained in the promotion record: a real finding, a false positive fixed in the code or config, or an exclusion with its reason

stable.enforce: after beta, the add-on runs in its acting mode (enforce / quarantine; armed) on that host for at least 30 consecutive days, every alert explained as for beta, with no unexplained kill, repair or quarantine
stable.recovery_drill: a recovery drill is done and recorded: undo one of its actions (restore a quarantined sample or repaired file from evidence, or roll the add-on back per docs/ADDONS.md 'Upgrade and rollback') and confirm the host is back to normal

requirements.check-config: a check-config command; acting commands refuse a config with errors (exit 78)
requirements.hardened-unit: every unit sandboxed; systemd-analyze security exposure at most max_exposure
requirements.resource-limits: MemoryMax= and TasksMax= on every unit
requirements.threat-model: a threat model section in docs/ADDONS.md
requirements.upgrade-rollback: upgrade and rollback steps in docs/ADDONS.md
requirements.baseline-trust: baselines and backups verified against a trust source the host cannot rewrite unnoticed
requirements.evidence-preserved: quarantine and repair keep the original bytes and hashes as evidence
requirements.adversarial-tests: malicious input, concurrent replacement, symlink race, stale/modified baseline, storage exhaustion and monitor-to-enforce tests
requirements.promotion-approved: the operator approved the promotion criteria and this add-on meets them
requirements.host-soak: run in monitor/log mode on a real host for the soak period in the criteria with no false positive left unexplained

procguard.acts: kills processes that are not on the allowlist; removes a respawning executable outside the system directories
procguard.na_why: its allowlist is operator input, not a recorded baseline of the host

tamperwatch.acts: in quarantine mode, kills the process that wrote a protected file after compressing its executable
tamperwatch.na_why: it watches writes as they happen; it keeps no baseline

driverguard.acts: in enforce mode, overwrites a changed kernel module file with its backup

bootguard.default_mode_note: enforce only stages a restore; it is applied at the next boot, and neither the timer nor the restore unit is enabled by the installer
bootguard.acts: at the next boot, overwrites changed /boot files with their backups

biosguard.acts: nothing: detection, log and notify only
biosguard.na_why: it never quarantines or repairs anything

locus.acts: nothing destructive: hands out directory names and creates its bucket directories
locus.na_why: it keeps no baseline and changes no files but its bucket directories

gui.acts: edits the add-on configs (rolled back if check-config fails), runs scans and baselines, quarantines a process on request

secure-sudo-gui.service.why: its children (scans, repairs, secure-sudo set, quarantine) inherit the sandbox

gui.na_why: it keeps no baseline; the guards it runs do

failure.acts: nothing: logs, ships and notifies that another add-on unit failed
failure.na_why: it has no settings of its own (logging.conf is checked by every guard), keeps no baseline, and is itself the failure reporting (a failing report must not start another)

pheonixbox.configs_note: its protected-path list is /etc/secure_sudo/pheonixbox.conf, managed with add/remove
pheonixbox.acts: when enabled, makes protected files read-only and repairs a changed one from its stored copy on each scan
pheonixbox.units_note: no unit of its own: secure-sudod runs `scan --quiet` on a timer, so it runs under the core daemon's unit
pheonixbox.na_why: it is part of the core release: it runs inside secure-sudod's unit and is upgraded and rolled back with install.sh
pheonixbox.open_note: baseline-trust: the snapshot is trusted as the host's own copy (no signed snapshot yet)
